Download PDF

Computational Science and Engineering student at ETH Zürich working on robot learning and at the intersection of machine learning and physics. At the Robotic Systems Lab I work on world models for contact-rich manipulation, using differentiable simulation with smoothed contact, and at the ETH Robotics Club I train whole-body control policies for a humanoid robot. Before that, I developed state-space sequence models for low-latency detection of gravitational-wave signals. I also have several years of experience shipping full-stack software as a freelancer and have taught courses on algorithms, data structures and software engineering.

2Research

Fall 2026 – presentWorld Models for Contact-Rich Robotics
Semester Project, Robotic Systems Lab (RSL), ETH Zürich

Joint semester project with Tristan Gabl on world models for contact-rich robot manipulation, with robot cloth folding as the target task.

  • Working on world models for contact-rich tasks, from latent and particle-based models to differentiable physics.
  • Investigating soft contact gradients to make differentiable simulators (MJX) usable as world models corrected from real data.
Fall 2026 – presentHumanoid Robot Learning
Humanoid Team, ETH Robotics Club

Learned whole-body control for the club’s humanoid robot, from training in simulation to deployment on the robot.

  • Trained a whole-body walking and teleoperation policy for the club’s 22-DoF humanoid in under one GPU hour, robust to the real robot’s sensor noise and latency.
  • Online demo: walk the humanoid with the trained policy in the browser (WASD)

June 2025 – Summer 2026AI for Gravitational-Wave Physics
ML Research Intern, Computational Applied Mathematics & AI Lab (CAMAIL)
ELLIS Institute Tübingen and Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, in collaboration with the LIGO Lab at MIT supervised by T. Konstantin Rusch.

Gravitational-wave signals can last minutes and are buried in non-stationary, glitchy detector noise, while astronomers need an alert within seconds to point telescopes at the merger. I worked on Linear Oscillatory State-Space Models (LinOSS): sequence models that handle very long inputs efficiently and towards making it possible to detect binary neutron star mergers in real time.

  • Designed and trained state-space models for low-latency binary neutron star detection on LIGO strain data.
  • Built the training and evaluation pipeline in PyTorch (Lightning) and JAX/Equinox.
  • Core contributor to Discretax, the lab’s open-source library of state-space models in JAX.
  • Co-developed PhyTS, a benchmark of physics time-series tasks (NeurIPS 2026).

Results appeared at NeurIPS 2026 [1] and were presented at AI for Gravitational Waves Workshop (CERN, Geneva) [2] and Fast Machine Learning for Science Conference 2026 (UC San Diego) [3].

5Teaching

6Projects

Presio: presio.ch · GitHub

Web app for presenting PDF slides with a presenter controller and a mirrored audience window. PDFs stay in the browser by default; signed-in users can share a session code so others can follow live on their own devices. Since its launch in September 2026 it has had over 2,000 users.

AcceptOdds: acceptodds.com · GitHub

A prediction market for research papers, launched on the ICLR 2027 submissions. Researchers with an institutional email trade each paper’s outcome (Accept/Reject) with a non-convertible play currency. Prices come from a logarithmic market scoring rule (LMSR). Since launching at the end of September 2026 it has had about 54,000 unique visitors from 96 countries and over 600,000 page views.
